lines: Every plank on this road was carried out here on somebody's shoulder.
You are welcome to walk on it. You are not welcome to call it a path.
A path is what the ground does. This is what we do instead of ground.
I ring it at dusk and I ring it for anybody late, and lately I ring it a lot.
There are more people on this road this season than in the nine years before it.
None of them are going to Mirehaven. They stop at the Rock and they go down.
You will not see the Waystation from the road. That is what the bell is for.
Two strokes on the hour. If you are lost, stand still and count them.
People try to walk toward a sound in fog. Do not. Walk at it. There is a difference.
Fifty years my family has poled this reach and I have never once seen the far bank.
You get to know a place by its bottom instead. Where it is firm, where it is not.
I could take you across blind. I could not draw you a map of it to save my life.
Foundation work. Ground survey, pile depths, water table, all of it above board.
No, I do not know what for. I take the readings and somebody else reads them.
They only want the numbers from one place, though. Right under the Rock.
Foundation survey. Depths and bearings. Do not touch the stakes, they are shot in.
Twelve of us came out. Nine went on to the town. I am the one who counts piles.
Fourteen posts in, fourteen posts back out, every evening of my life.
People thank me for the light. The light is not the point of it.
The point is that if a lamp is out when I get to it, somebody has been at it.
